messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: transformed parameters & Jacobians
parts:
Some of the BUGS models (like epil.stan) have
problems in that parameters are getting transformed and
sampled without Jacobians being applied. I almost certainly
committed the original sin with RATS.

I fixed rats.stan, but not epil.stan and haven't looked
for other cases.

Here's an instance of the right way to deal with gamma
priors on precision (inverse gamma priors on variance)
in Stan.

// GOOD PROGRM
parameters {
double(0,) sigma_sq;
}
transformed parameters {
double(0,) sigma;
sigma <- sqrt(sigma_sq);
}
model {
sigma_sq ~ inv_gamma(0.001, 0.001);

for (n in 1:N)
y[n] ~ normal(mu,sigma);
}

It's OK to sample a parameter

sigma_sq ~ inf_gamma(...);

and then transform it for use

sigma <- sqrt(sigma_sq);

y[n] ~ normal(mu,sigma);

We wind up with:

p(sigma_sq,y) prop-to
InvGamma(sigma_sq|0.001,0.001)
* PROD_n Normal(y|mu,sqrt(sigma_sq))

Remember that all parameters and transformed parameters
are output. If you don't want to see the sigma in
the output, but only the sigma_sq, define sigma as a local
variable in the model rather than as a transformed parameter.
The effect on sampling and computation is exactly the same, only
the I/O changes. (I'm afraid there's no way to only write
sigma and not sigma_sq here w/o applying the Jacobian manually.)

But it's NOT OK to do it the other way around:

// BAD PROGRAM
parameters {
double(0,) sigma;
}
transformed parameters {
double(0,) sigma_sq;
sigma_sq <- square(sigma_sq);
}
model {
sigma_sq ~ inv_gamma(0.001, 0.001);

for (n in 1:N)
y[n] ~ normal(mu,sigma);
}

It's legal to transform and sample the transformed
parameter, but ONLY if you apply the appropriate
Jacobian determinant. The bad program leads to

p(sigma,y) NOT prop-to
InvGamma(square(sigma)|0.001,0.001)
* PROD_n Normal(y|mu,sigma)

This model could be fixed by applying the Jacobian of
the inverse of transform:

p_sigma(sigma)
= p_sigma_sq(square(sigma_sq)) * | d/dx square(sigma) |

which translates into Stan as another statement for the
transformed parameters block:

lp__ <- lp__ + log(2 * sigma);

or more efficiently as:

lp__ <- lp__ + log2() + log(sigma);

(I just added constants like log2() yesterday.)

This very prevalent use case would motivate an alternative
parameterization of inverse gamma so we could just write:

sigma ~ square_inv_gamma(0.001,0.001)

- Bob
